claims.text: A thin molybdenum interlayer can be placed between tungsten and CuCrZr.
A molybdenum interlayer will reduce interfacial stress between tungsten and CuCrZr.
A molybdenum interlayer will limit interdiffusion between tungsten and CuCrZr under fusion-reactor operating conditions.
A direct W-to-CuCrZr interface may be prone to interdiffusion.
A direct W-to-CuCrZr interface may be prone to thermal-mismatch stresses.
Fusion-reactor components encounter high temperature, high heat flux, and high radiation.
Molybdenum has a thermal-expansion coefficient intermediate between those of tungsten and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has a high melting temperature.
The molybdenum layer will act as a diffusion barrier between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The molybdenum layer will act as a mechanical or thermal buffer zone between tungsten and CuCrZr.
Moderating thermal-expansion differences with molybdenum will enhance mechanical bonding in the composite.
Impeding atomic interdiffusion with molybdenum will enhance the composite's thermal stability under extreme conditions.
A W/Mo/CuCrZr composite will exhibit less interfacial degradation during thermal cycling than a direct W/CuCrZr interface.
A W/Mo/CuCrZr composite will exhibit less diffusion-induced weakening during thermal cycling than a direct W/CuCrZr interface.
A W/Mo/CuCrZr composite will retain better mechanical integrity during thermal cycling than a direct W/CuCrZr interface.
Interdiffusion and stress accumulation at a direct W/CuCrZr interface can lead to premature failure.
The proposed applicability is limited to layered composites in nuclear-fusion-reactor environments.
The performance of the molybdenum interlayer under fusion-reactor conditions remains to be experimentally validated.
